name: Preacher Curl
description: The preacher curl is a biceps curl variation performed with the upper arms resting on an angled arm pad, which prevents elbow movement and places the biceps under constant tension. The preacher bench position provides a greater stretch on the long head of the biceps at the bottom and prevents cheating with the torso.

execution.starting_position: Sit at the preacher bench with the upper arms resting flat on the angled pad. Hold an EZ-curl bar or dumbbells with a supinated or semi-supinated grip. Arms nearly fully extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust the bench seat height so the upper arms lie flat on the pad with the armpits at the top edge of the pad.
steps: Curl the bar upward by flexing the elbows, keeping the upper arms in contact with the pad.
Raise until full biceps contraction is achieved.
Lower slowly and under control — the eccentric portion is especially important here.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on descent.
common_mistakes: Lifting the upper arms off the pad to gain leverage
Not lowering to full extension, missing the stretch
safety_considerations: The preacher position can stress the distal biceps tendon at full extension — control the descent
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Near-full extension at the bottom (avoid hyperextension), full contraction at the top.
coaching_cues: Keep the upper arms welded to the pad
Control the descent — do not let the bar drop
